header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tlg0533.tlg015.perseus-grc3, from the Perseus Digital Library (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. nodes.text: than the god himself, ever great, ever lord,
driver-off of the Pelagones, giver of justice to the sons of Heaven?
And how shall we sing him, as Dictaean or as Lycaean?
My heart is much in doubt, since his birth is disputed.
Zeus, some say you were born in the Idaean mountains,
Zeus, others in Arcadia; which of them, father, lied?
Cretans are always liars; for indeed a tomb, O lord, for you
the Cretans built; but you did not die, for you are forever.
In Parrhasia Rhea bore you, where most of all
the mountain was thickly covered with shrubs; hence the place
is holy, and nothing in need of Eileithyia,
the Dictaean Meliae, and Adrasteia lulled you to sleep
in a golden cradle, and you sucked the rich teat
of the she-goat Amaltheia, and besides you ate sweet honeycomb.
For suddenly the works of the Panacrian bee appeared
on the Idaean mountains, which they call Panacra.
And the Curetes danced the *prylis* [armed dance] around you loudly,
clashing their armour, so that Cronus might hear with his ears the din
of the shield, and not you crying as a baby.
did not grudge you having heaven as your appointed home.
The poets of old were not wholly truthful.
They said the lot divided the threefold houses among the sons of Cronus;
but who would draw lots for Olympus and for Hades,
